points.description: Sets up the casework correctly: for each side, P must satisfy one of three conditions (e.g. for BC: PB=PC, PB=BC, or PC=BC), and notes AB=AC so some loci coincide (circle centred A radius AB is shared by sides AB and CA). The case analysis is organised so that every combination is covered.

Finds the circumcenter O (all three perpendicular-bisector conditions; any two bisectors force P=O) as 1 point, and the points on the axis of symmetry: 2 points with PA=AB (on the axis, one above A and one below, near BC) and 2 points with PB=PC=AB (on the axis, one above and one below BC). This gives 5 points.
points.partial_credit: Half of this mark if most of these points are found but one family (e.g. the axis/PA=AB or PB=PC=AB points) is missed or miscounted.

points.description: Finds the 2 points from PA=AB=AC together with PB=BC or PC=BC, namely the reflections of C over AB and of B over AC. Correctly excludes the degenerate solutions P=B and P=C.

Shows that all other combinations are impossible, using the triangle inequality or distance estimates such as AB=AC≈0.5/0.17≈2.94 times BC, and that the apex-type points of equilateral triangles on AB or AC are not at distance BC from B or C. Also checks that the listed points are distinct and non-degenerate.

rubric.notes: The full mark answer is 7, with valid casework. The model answer gave no working or final value, so this scheme uses the worked-out answer 7. Equivalent methods and wording are accepted. A wrong final count earns at most the casework marks.
rubric.answer_key: Answer: 7. Take BC=1, so AB=AC=L≈0.5/cos80≈2.94. For each side P must satisfy one of three conditions. Two perpendicular-bisector conditions force P to be the circumcenter O (1 point). On the axis of symmetry, PA=AB gives 2 points and PB=PC=AB gives 2 points (4 points). PA=AB with PB=BC or PC=BC gives the reflections of C over AB and of B over AC (2 points), after excluding the degenerate P=B and P=C. All other combinations are impossible. Total 1+4+2=7.
